findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
(c) 2-401.11 Employee was chewing gum while working in the kitchen. Gum was discarded at request of inspector.
Employees shall eat, including gum/candy, only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single service and single use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
(P) 4-501.114 Quat solution in sani-buckets was observed at 0ppm at front service line/prep area and 100ppm in back by 3 part sink. Fresh solutions at 200ppm were provided.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solution in the front service line sani-bucket was observed at 100ppm. All other solutions were at 200ppm. Fresh solution was provided at 200ppm. Allow dispenser to run for several seconds and ensure chemical is moving through the suction line prior to filing buckets and 3 part sink. Use test strips to verify concentration.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-501.15 Rinse gauge of dish machine was reading at 120F after ware washing cycles were completed. Wash gauge was reading at ~164F, and dish temp tester showed the final rinse surface temperature to be at 160F and 162F for consecutive cycles. After five more cycles the rinse gauge read at 140F. Kitchen manager will have maintenance check the machine and call for outside service if maintenance is unable to fix the issue. 
A warewashing machine and its auxiliary components shall be operated in accordance with the machine's data plate and other manufacturer's instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The dish machine food contact surface temperature was observed at 154 F. The rinse temperature was observed at approximately 130F, and the wash temperature was observed at approximately 155F. The dish machine must achieve a minimum food-contact surface temperature of 160F. Ensure the dish machine is serviced so that can be achieved. Dishes may still be washed in the dish machine, but dishes must be sanitized in the 3 part sink. The manager stated that dishes will be sanitized in the 3 part sink until the dish machine is sanitizing properly. 

4-703.11: After cleaning, FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be SANITIZED in: (A) manual hot water operations. (B) mechanical hot water operations. (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use  standard contact time 30 seconds.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on fans in walk-in cooler. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Student worker was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off with bare hands prior to retrieving paper towels. Worker was observed using a forearm to dispense paper towels. Worker was advised to use a forearm to shut off the faucet as well or use paper towels as a barrier once hands are dry to shut off the faucet in order to avoid potential re-contamination of freshly washed hands.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated and prior to working with food and clean equipment.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the caulk in the dish room to be cracked and separating from the wall. Re-caulk tables in the dish room to the wall.
750-1210e  Equipment attached to walls and ceilings shall be easily cleanable and shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed sour cream in the walk in cooler to be probed at an internal temperature of 44F as probed with a recently calibrated digital thermometer. Staff has noticed fluctuation in the temperature of the unit with the weather change and maintenance adjusted unit last week and was called during inspection to adjust unit today. Daily temperature log for the month of January was reviewed and staff will monitor temperature this week and fax inspector the temperatures at the end of the week. Maintain internal temperatures of 41F or below.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed a scoop handle stored in contact with the sugar in the bulk sugar container. Store scoops with handles extended up and out of the food.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the caulk at the three compartment sink to have gaps along the wall. Scrape old caulk off and recaulk sink to the wall.
750-1210(b) Walls and ceilings in walk-in refrigeration units, food preparation areas, equipment washing areas, and toilet rooms shall be smooth, light-cored, non-absorbant, and easily cleanable. Concrete or pumice block in these locations shall be finished and sealed to provide a cleanable surface.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the front serving counters to have some areas of worn or exposed particle board. All non-food contact surfaces should be smooth, nonabsorbent and easily cleanable.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
CORRECTED Observed a molded personal salad dressing bottle being stored on a shelf above food served to the students. Item was discarded. Store all personal items away from and below all food served to the students to prevent possible contamination.
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
1) Observed the floor under the back shelving units in the walk-in cooler to be soiled black. Clean the floors. 2) Observed the floor in the dry storage room in front of the walk-in freezer to be cracked, peeling, and chipping. Reseal the floor so they are smooth and easily cleanable.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.
